spans.s:
बर बर, अस्, m. a N. of Bala-rāma (=
बल).

बार बार, Ved. an opening, aperture; [cf.
जिह्म-ब्˚, नीचीन-ब्˚.]

बरट बरट, अस्, m. a species of grain;
[cf. बर्बट.]

बरासी बरासी, f. a particular article of
clothing or kind of woven cloth; (also read वरासी,
वरासि, वराशि.)

बरु बरु, उस्, m., Ved., N. of a descendant
of Aṅgiras and author of the hymn Ṛg-veda

;
N. of an Āṅgirasa.
बरोदा बरोदा, N. of a place in Guzerat.

बर्कु बर्कु, उस्, m., Ved., N. of a man
with the patronymic Vārṣṇa.
बर्जर बर्जर, N. of a place.

बर्जह बर्जह, अस्, अम्, m. n., Ved. an
udder, (Sāy. = पयस उत्पत्ति-स्थानम्.)
बर्जह्य, अम्, n., Ved. a nipple.

बर्ब् बर्ब्, cl. 1. P. बर्बति, बर्बितुम्, to
go, move.

बर्बट बर्बट, अस्, ई, m. f. a kind of bean,
Dolichos Catjang [cf. बरट]; (ई), f. a harlot, pros-
titute; [cf. बार्बटीर.]

बर्बणा बर्बणा, f. (said to be fr. rt. बर्ब्),
a blue fly.

बर्बर बर्बर, अस्, m. (also written वर्-
वर, q. v., cf. βάρβαρος), a blockhead, fool, low fel-
low, barbarian, any one not a Sanskrit speaker, not an
Āryan, (used mostly in the voc.); (अस् or अम्), m.
or n. (?), N. of a district.
—बर्बर-ता, f. (in Ved.
gram.) a stammering pronunciation of the letter र्.
—बर्बर-स्थान, N. of a district.
बर्बरक, बर्बरीक. See वर्वरक, &c.

बर्बुर बर्बुर, अम्, n., Ved. water; [cf.
Gr. βόρβορο-ν; Fr. bourbe.]

बर्स बर्स, अस्, m., Ved. a tip, point, thin
end, extremity.
—बर्स-नद्धि, इस्, f., Ved. the
tying of sacrificial knots.

बर्स्व बर्स्व, अस्, m., Ved. the fleshy forma-
tion of the gums round the socket of a tooth, a
socket of a tooth.

बर्ह् बर्ह् (also written वर्ह्, q. v., cf.
rts. बृह्, वृह्, बृंह्, वृंह्), cl. 1. A.
बर्हते, बबर्हे, बर्हितुम्, to speak; to hurt,
injure, kill; to give, (according to another reading)
to cover; to spread, (this sense being perhaps only
deduced from बर्हिस्, q. v.); to be pre-eminent or
excellent; cl. 10. P. बर्हयति, to hurt, injure, kill.
बर्ह बर्ह, बर्हिन्. See वर्ह, वर्हिन्.
बार्ह बार्ह, बार्हिण. See वार्ह.

बर्हण बर्हण (fr. rt. बृंह् for वृंह्), Ved.
strong; occurring only in the Vedic inst. बर्हणा,
closely, firmly, strongly; very, really, certainly.
—बर्हण-वत्, आन्, अती, अत्, energetic, vigorous,
earnest; (according to Sāy.) injuring enemies.
—बर्-
हणाश्व (˚ण-अश्˚), अस्, m., N. of a prince, a son
of Nikumbha.

बर्हस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, Ved. strong, firm; occurring
only in अद्रि-बर्हस्, आस्, आस्, अस्, firm as a rock,
fastened by rocks; (or according to Sāy.) spread out
or swollen with clouds, and in द्वि-ब्˚, q. v.

1. बर्हिष्ठ, अस्, आ, अम्, strongest, &c. See वर्-
हिष्ठ. (For 2. बर्हि-ष्ठ see p. 675, col. 1.)

बर्हिस् बर्हिस्, इस्, m. n. (in the later litera-
ture generally written वर्हिस्; probably fr. rt. 1. or 2.
वृह्; said to be fr. rt. वृंह्), (that which is plucked
up), a bed or layer of Kuśa grass (usually strewed
over the sacrificial ground and especially over the
Vedi, to serve as a sacred surface on which to present
[]
the oblations, and as a seat for the gods and for the
sacrificers); Kuśa grass, sacrificial grass; (इस्), n. the
strewed sacrificial grass personified and enumerated
among the Pra-yāja and Anu-yāja deities; sacrifice
(= तन्त्र); ether; water; a kind of perfume, =
बर्हि-पुष्प; (इस्), m. fire, light, lustre, splendor;
Plumbago Zeylanica (to which plant all the names
of fire are applied); N. of a son of Bṛhad-rāja;
(इषस्), m. pl. the descendants of Barhis.
—बर्हिः-
पुष्प, अम्, n. = बर्हि-पुष्प.
—बर्हिः-शुष्-
मन्, आ, m. fire, the god of fire.
—बर्हिः-षद्,
see under बर्हि-षद्.
—बर्हिः-ष्ठ, अस्, m.
‘standing upon the sacrificial grass,’ (perhaps) a
victim; (अम्), n. a kind of perfume commonly
called Bāla; or (according to some) a kind of fragrant
grass, Andropogon Muricatus.
—बर्हिः-ष्ठा, आस्,
आस्, अम्, Ved. standing or placed upon the sacrificial
grass.
—बर्हि-कुसुम, अम्, n. = बर्हि-पुष्प.
—बर्हि-पुष्प, अम्, n. a kind of perfume.
—बर्-
हिर्-ज्योतिस्, इस्, m. fire, the deity of fire.
—बर्हिर्-
मुख, अस्, m. ‘fire-mouthed,’ a deity (so called
because sacrifices are mostly offered to the gods by
fire).
—बर्हि-षद्, त्, त्, त् (बर्हि for बर्हिस् + सद्),
seated on sacrificial grass; (according to the Nirukta)
= महत्, great; (दस्), m. pl. the Manes; (in the
later literature) a particular class of Pitṛs or Manes,
see Manu

; (त्), m. a Pitṛ or deified
progenitor; N. of a son of Havir-dhāna and Havir-
dhānī (= प्राचीन-बर्हिस्).
—बर्हि-षद, अस्, m.,
N. of a holy sage (= बर्हिन्).
—बर्हिष्-केश, अस्,
m. ‘having light for hair,’ fire, Agni, the god of fire.
 — 2. बर्हि-ष्ठ, अम्, n. a kind of fragrant grass
or perfume; the resin of the Pinus Longifolia, see
बर्हिः-ष्ठ; (for 1. बर्हिष्ठ see p. 674,
col. 3.)
—बर्हिष्-मत्, आन्, अती, अत्, possessing
sacrificial grass, (Sāy. = आस्तीर्णेन बर्हिषा युक्-
तः); (आन्), m. one who has or spreads sacrificial
grass, a worshipper, sacrificer, (Sāy. = यज्ञेन युक्-
तः); having fire or light, blazing, shining; (आन्),
m. an epithet of Prācīna-barhis; (अती), f., N. of a
wife of Priya-vrata and daughter of Viśva-karman;
N. of a city in Brahmāvarta.

बर्हिष्क, अस्, आ, अम्, formed of sacrificial grass;
covered with sacrificial grass; a perfume commonly
called Bāla, (perhaps a species of Andropogon); resin
of Pinus Longifolia; (also written बर्हिस्क.)
बर्हिस्क = बर्हिष्क above.

बर्हिष्य, अस्, आ, अम्, Ved. belonging to or fitted
for sacrificial grass; कश्यपस्य बर्हिष्यम्, N. of
a Sāman.

बारहट बारहट, अस्, m. epithet of Nara-
hara-dāsa the author of the Hindī work Avatāra-
caritra or Caturviṃsaty-avatāra-caritra.
बारेज्य बारेज्य, N. of a town.

बार्बटीर बार्बटीर or बार्वटीर, अस्, m. the
kernel of the mango fruit; a young shoot; tin; the
son of a harlot; [cf. बर्बटी.]

बार्हत बार्हत, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. बृहत्), Ved.
relating to the Sāman called Bṛhat, celebrated in the
Bṛhat-sāman, (according to Mahī-dhara = बृहत्-
साम-स्तुत); relating or belonging to the Bṛhatī
metre, representing it, consisting of it; बार्हतं
वाजजिदौक्ष्णोरन्ध्रम्, N. of a Sāman; (अम्),
n. the fruit of the Bṛhatī, a variety of the So-
lanum.

बार्हतानुष्टुभ, अस्, ई, अम् (fr. बृहत् + अनु-
ष्टुभ्), Ved. consisting of a Bṛhatī and an Anu-
ṣṭubh.

बार्हत्सामा, f. (fr. बृहत्-सामन्), Ved., N. or
epithet of a woman.

बार्हदग्न, आस्, m. pl. (fr. बृहद्-अग्नि), the
descendants of Bṛhad-agni.

बार्हदीषव, अस्, m. a patronymic from Bṛhad-
ishu (with इ lengthened).

बार्हदुक्थ, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. relating or be-
longing to Bṛhad-uktha; (अस्), m. a patronymic
from Bṛhad-uktha.

बार्हद्गिर, अस्, ई, अम्, Ved. relating or belong-
ing to Bṛhad-giri.

बार्हद्दैवत, अम्, n. (fr. बृहद्-देवता),
N. of a work also called Bṛhad-devatā and attributed
to Śaunaka.

बार्हद्बल, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to
Bṛhad-bala.

बार्हद्रथि, इस्, m. (fr. बृहद्-रथ), a patro-
nymic of Jarā-sandha.

बार्हवत, अस्, ई, अम्, containing the word बर्ह-
वत्.

बार्हस्पत, अस्, ई, अम्, relating or belonging to
Bṛhas-pati, descended from Bṛhas-pati, sacred to
Bṛhas-pati.

बार्हस्पत्य, अस्, ती, अम्, relating to or coming
from Bṛhas-pati; (अस्), m. a pupil of Bṛhas-pati;
an infidel, a materialist; an epithet of Śamyu; of
[]
Agni; of Tapur-mūrdhan; of Bharad-vāja; (अम्),
n., scil. भ or नक्षत्र, the constellation Puṣya;
the Artha-śāstra of Bṛhas-pati, ethics, morality;
बार्हस्पत्यम् मानम्, ‘Jupiter's measure of
time,’ a method of reckoning time.
—बार्हस्पत्य-
ज्योतिर्-ग्रन्थ, अस्, m., N. of a work mentioned
in Raghu-nandana's Saṃskāra-tattva.
—बार्हस्प-
त्य-तन्त्र, अम्, n., N. of a Tantra mentioned in
the Ānanda-laharī.

बार्हिषद बार्हिषद, अस्, m. a patronymic
from Barhiṣad.
